# ddr_mem: generation prompt

```text
Create a new SystemVerilog IP block for the FPGA Cores 4 U digital IP library.
```

## 1. Identity

- Module name: `ddr_mem`
- Library category: `memory`
- Location: `ip/memory/ddr_mem/`
- One-line purpose: Generic DDR memory for simulation (a behavioural model of an external SDRAM, not synthesizable logic) behind a DFI-style command interface, one command per clock (controller clock = DFI clock, 1:1), w
- Version: 1.0.0

## 2. Context

- Where it is used: standalone library block.
- Existing IP to reuse (do not duplicate): none; self-contained.

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Meaning / legal range |
|---|---|---|
| `DATA_W` | `256` | bits per column word (multiple of 8) |
| `BANK_W` | `3` | log2 banks |
| `ROW_W` | `14` | row address bits |
| `COL_W` | `8` | column (word) address bits |
| `MEM_WORDS` | `1 << 16` | words stored |
| `T_RCD` | `4` | ACT to RD / WR |
| `T_RP` | `4` | PRE to ACT (and to REF) |
| `T_RAS` | `10` | ACT to PRE |
| `T_CL` | `5` | RD to data |
| `T_WR` | `4` | WR to PRE |
| `T_RTP` | `2` | RD to PRE |
| `T_WTR` | `2` | WR to RD |
| `T_RRD` | `2` | ACT to ACT (any banks) |
| `T_RFC` | `30` | REF to the next command |
| `REF_MAX` | `9 * 1950` | longest time without a REF |

Reject illegal values at elaboration with `$error` inside a generate block.

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`, `wrstrb_i`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

| Port | Dir | Width | Group | Built when | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clk` | input | 1 | - | - | clock |
| `rst_n` | input | 1 | - | - | synchronous, active low |
| `cmd_i` | input | [2:0] | - | - | command (see the header) |
| `bank_i` | input | [BANK_W-1:0] | - | - | bank of ACT / RD / WR / PRE |
| `row_i` | input | [ROW_W-1:0] | - | - | row of ACT |
| `col_i` | input | [COL_W-1:0] | - | - | column of RD / WR |
| `wrdata_i` | input | [DATA_W-1:0] | - | - | WR data |
| `wrstrb_i` | input | [DATA_W/8-1:0] | - | - | WR byte enables |
| `rddata_valid_o` | output | 1 | - | - | a RD's word (T_CL clocks after it) |
| `rddata_o` | output | [DATA_W-1:0] | - | - | the word |
| `err_o` | output | 1 | - | - | sticky: a timing / protocol violation |
| `err_code_o` | output | [3:0] | - | - | the first violation's code |
| `err_cnt_o` | output | [15:0] | - | - | clocks with a violation |

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Generic DDR memory for simulation (a behavioural model of an
external SDRAM, not synthesizable logic) behind a DFI-style command
interface, one command per clock (controller clock = DFI clock, 1:1),
with the timing checks of a JEDEC SDRAM. Version 1.0.0. Golden model:
model/ddr_mem_model.py (clock exact; tb/python).
- Commands (cmd_i): 0 NOP, 1 ACT (open row_i in bank_i), 2 RD (bank_i,
  col_i), 3 WR (bank_i, col_i, wrdata_i, the bytes with wrstrb_i set),
  4 PRE (close bank_i; a no-op for a closed bank), 5 PREA (close every
  bank), 6 REF (refresh; every bank closed), 7 illegal.
- Word address: {open row, bank, col} = (row << (BANK_W + COL_W)) |
  (bank << COL_W) | col; it must be below MEM_WORDS. Unwritten words
  read 0; a RD / WR to a closed bank or beyond MEM_WORDS reads 0 /
  writes nothing.
- A RD in clock n gives rddata_valid_o with the word in clock n + T_CL
  (the word before a WR of the same clock).
- Timing checks (ages in clocks since a bank's last ACT / PRE / WR / RD
  and since the last ACT, WR, REF of any bank, saturating at 255; every
  timing parameter 1 .. 254): 1 ACT to an open bank, 2 RD / WR to a
  closed bank, 3 RD / WR before T_RCD, 4 ACT before T_RP after the
  bank's PRE or REF before T_RP after any PRE, 5 PRE before T_RAS, 6 PRE
  before T_WR after a WR or T_RTP after a RD, 7 ACT before T_RRD after
  any ACT, 8 RD before T_WTR after any WR, 9 REF with a bank open, 10 a
  command before T_RFC after a REF, 11 refresh overdue (more than
  REF_MAX clocks since reset or the last REF; once until the next REF),
  12 address beyond MEM_WORDS, 13 illegal command. PREA checks 5 / 6 for
  every open bank. The command is still applied.
- err_o (sticky) at the first violation, err_code_o the smallest code of
  that clock, err_cnt_o the clocks with a violation (saturating).
Parameters: DATA_W (multiple of 8), BANK_W, ROW_W, COL_W, MEM_WORDS (the
words stored), the timings in clocks, REF_MAX.
Clock - clk. Reset - synchronous active low rst_n (bank state, checks,
read pipeline; the contents are kept). Clock-domain crossings - none.
Latency - read data T_CL clocks after the RD; all outputs registered.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - ddr_mem (2026-10-21)
// Sources:
//   [1] JEDEC, "DDR4 SDRAM Standard", JESD79-4 (2012-2021), https://www.jedec.org/standards-documents/docs/jesd79-4a
//   - 4.x command truth table (ACT, RD, WR, PRE, PREA, REF), timing parameters tRCD, tRP, tRAS, tRTP, tWR,
//   tWTR, tRRD, tRFC, tREFI (up to 8 refreshes may be postponed)
//   [2] DFI Group, "DDR PHY Interface (DFI) Specification" 5.0 (2018), https://www.ddr-phy.org - command
//   interface (dfi_address, dfi_bank, dfi_ras_n / cas_n / we_n, dfi_cs), write data (dfi_wrdata, _en,
//   _mask, tphy_wrlat), read data (dfi_rddata, _valid, trddata_en, tphy_rdlat)
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   A bank must be activated before RD / WR (tRCD later), stays open until PRE (tRAS after ACT, tWR
//   after the last write data, tRTP after a RD), may be activated again tRP after the PRE; ACTs to
//   different banks tRRD apart; a RD tWTR after write data; REF with every bank precharged, nothing for
//   tRFC; on average one REF per tREFI, at most 8 postponed (9 x tREFI between two REFs).
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: the command set, every listed timing rule, refresh deadline REF_MAX = 9 x tREFI by
//   default, open-row per bank, byte write masks. Simplifications (deliberate, simulation model of the
//   generic build): one encoded cmd field instead of ras_n / cas_n / we_n / cs_n; write data with the WR
//   command (tphy_wrlat 0) and read data T_CL clocks after RD (the controller's view after the PHY's
//   latencies); one data word per command (the burst folded into DATA_W, a 1:1 DFI frequency ratio);
//   no mode registers, ZQ calibration, ODT or tFAW; the timing violations are reported (err_o) instead of
//   corrupting data.
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: report the Yosys utilisation; keep it in line with similar library blocks.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking directed testbench for ddr_mem (small
configuration: 32-bit words, 4 banks, T_CL 3). Checks, independently of
the Python model: written words read back T_CL clocks after RD, partial
byte strobes, unwritten words read 0, rows kept per bank, and that each
timing rule (tRCD, tRP, tRAS, tWR, tRFC, a closed bank, the refresh
deadline) sets err_o with its code. The exact clock-by-clock comparison
with the model is tb/python. Test tasks in tests/ddr_mem_tests.sv.
Prints TEST PASSED on success.
```

There is also a Python (cocotb) test in `tb/python/`; provide an equivalent.

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh ddr_mem --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `ddr_mem_tb` | `test_write_read` | Writes and reads back over two banks and rows, partial strobes, unwritten words read 0 |
| `ddr_mem_tb` | `test_timing_checks` | Each of tRCD, tRP, tRAS, tWR, tRFC and a closed bank sets err_o with its code |
| `ddr_mem_tb` | `test_refresh_deadline` | No REF for REF_MAX clocks sets code 11 |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C memory/ddr_mem test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
